Does it use associations or how does it find the PowerWatts?
I've updated the commit message to specify how the association is being used.
Done
Redfish.md update?
ERROR please
Done
Do we need any unit tests for this?
FYI. I'm going to start working on addressing the code review comments of this commit and the other unmerged commits for this same topic.
I've added the environmentMetricsNode to the relevant unit tests.
you implemented more than one property here.  Please document appropriately.  I see at the very least DataSourceUri and Reading
Done
why do we call getSubTree, THEN getObject?  I suspect the subtree call can be removed entirely?
I've restructured the flow which simplifies things. I've updated the commit message with the new flow.
Done

This is getting all sensors for the whole system, not just for this chassis.  As written, this will respond with a PowerWatts object on every chassis.  Do we need a test to verify that behavior doesn't exist in the future?
I've restructured to use the new 'total_power' association for the chassis. I've updated the commit message to show the new flow.
Done
Need the new logging here {}
Done

Why are we looking for a specific name of a power sensor?  I realize there is code that does this already in the existing power schemas, but we know from experience that hardcoding specific sensor names is a bad idea, so I don't really want to accept new patches that make that behavior worse.
A new association here?
I've updated to use the new 'total_power' association from the chassis to the sensor. I've updated the commit message with the reference to the commit which added the new association.
Done
We call subtree, then we hardcode an object path?
I've restructured to use the new association, the path is no longer hard-coded. Please see commit message for new flow.
Done
https://github.com/openbmc/bmcweb/commit/c1d019a6056a2a0ef50e577b3139ab5a8dc49355 moved this over to power_total_power
I've modified to use sensor_utils::objectExcerptToJson(). This function builds the DataSourceUri in the standard way.
Done
It's a little odd we have @odata.id and DataSourceURI here.  are you sure that's correct?

You are right, that was not correct. From the schema definition @odata.id should not be here just the DataSourceUri is a defined property for SensorPowerExcerpt.

I've changed to use sensor_utils::objectExcerptToJson() which handles this correctly.
Done
This looks incorrect.  Can you verify that you tested this link produced was correct?
It was not correct. I've tested the link being produced now and the link does connect to the total_power sensor. See commit message for example.
Done
This lambda is 3 tiers deep.  as has been pointed out in the past, please don't write non trivial lambdas.
I've restructured to remove most of the lambdas and created named functions instead.
Done
It looks good to me
I think Doxygen uses `@details` - https://www.doxygen.nl/manual/commands.html
Thank you for catching this, I've corrected it.
Where is this documented though in PDI?
https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/+/75943 is the review

This has changed to use the Sensor.Purpose interface through the existing all_sensors association instead. Commit message has been updated to point to the commits which add and implement this interface.
It looks good to me
This seems reasonable based on what the backend documented
nit, sign offs together please.
Done
Waiting on https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/+/79619 here
That new PDI interface was rejected by the maintainer. Addressing review comments using merged PDI interface instead.
nlohmann::object_t item;

objectExcerptToJson() calls objectPropertiesToJson(), which takes a nlohmann::json& sensorJson. When I tried to chang this local variable to be of type nlohmann:object_t I got compile errors and could only pass it if I cast it. That seemed more problematic. Is there another way I could handle it?

https://github.com/openbmc/bmcweb/blob/da9dc905da4e6d30125bcca160537cf2cdb2ddf4/redfish-core/include/utils/sensor_utils.hpp#L402
Yep, you are right.  I tried to do the conversion to make this "correct", but hit some issues.  Fine as is.

I don't see any code handling for if there's multiple sensors that claim this interface.  As written, it looks like you'll just get whichever sensor answers second.

This is kind of an indirect version of common error #8:
https://github.com/openbmc/bmcweb/blob/master/COMMON_ERRORS.md#7-lack-of-locking-between-subsequent-calls
I'll address this along with changes based on the Sensor.Purpose discussion.

Question on this one: For the GET paths looking for a particular id, the common path is to accept the first one found that matches it and then just return.
E.g. https://github.com/openbmc/bmcweb/blob/da9dc905da4e6d30125bcca160537cf2cdb2ddf4/redfish-core/lib/fan.hpp#L181

So is that the expectation here as well? Or is it desired to return an error if there is more than one sensor that implements this purpose?

I modified to chain together the retrieval of the Sensor.Purpose values for the subset of sensors which could be implementing the TotalPower purpose. After determining the list of any or all sensors with the TotalPower purpose the callback is called to handle. It will error out if there is more than one sensor. Not an error if there are no sensors with this purpose.

I've updated the commit message to detail the new code flow.
Getting all sensors for a chassis to find a single one seems worrying.  Is there any way to avoid this (see discussion on discord).

I did try to limit the number of sensors pulled by specifying just power sensors. Additionally it is only going to pull the ones which implement the Sensor.Purpose interface. My expectation is that is a small list of just special purpose sensors.

On my system there are a total of 181 sensors associated to my <validChassisPath>. However doing this call only a single sensor is returned as there is only a single sensor implementing the Sensor.Purpose interface.
Over time there is potential other sensors will implement this interface to define special purposes. My expectation is that this will continue to be a small percentage of all the available sensors.
Ready for re-review. I've left one comment as unresolved to see if @ed@tanous.net agrees with my response.
Good point. I've restructured to take out the recursion. Thank you for the suggestion!
